reviews.title: Quality future proof budget friendly PSU
reviews.comment: My first impressions of Vetroo 1000W white PSU are very positive. It is fully modular, supports ATX 3.0 modern standard and has two PCIe 5.0 power ports with up to 600W power delivery for modern graphics cards (1 12VHPWR cable included). It also has smart fan technology to eliminate any fan noise at low power delivery. Ever popular Cultists PSU tier list puts this PSU in category B (recommended) and authoritative Hardware Busters reviews this PSU very positively, noting modern design, quality components and stable power. My PSU came with all white high quality cables (power cord is still black) in a nice presentation package and installing this PSU in the case was effortless with clearly marked ports and cables, so there is no confusion what cable should go where. Vetroo PSU powers hungry NVidia 4080 Super graphics card without a hitch using the included 12VHPWR cable and all stability stress tests ran without any problems. PSU is dead silent most of the time and when fan operates at high load it is very quiet and drowns in the noise of the case fans. Vetroo does not make this PSU, rather relying on the high reputation OEM manufacturer who also makes much more expensive SeaSonic and EVGA PSUs. Time will tell if this PSU is going to last, but for the price it is an unbeatable value in a sea of very expensive brand name PSU vendors.

reviews.comment: Looks good and works as advertised . Fully modular. I love the look in my build. I also use vetroo case fans and a vetroo cpu cooler....not disappointed with anything. Price is good
reviews.author: steve czachor

reviews.title: Good quality built power supply
reviews.comment: The power supply comes with 2 PCIe 5.1 display card adaptors which may be useful for new power hungry display cards.  The power supply is relatively lighter when holding on the hand.  The cables looks relatively narrower than those I used before. The cable coating is nylon feel which is very nice.  However I do not know if this is good or bad for slimmer cables: on the positive side easier cable management, on the negative side, the cables may be undersized. Overall I am still very satisfied with this power supply especially the built quality.  For performance, as I am not a demanding user with power hungry CPUs or display cards, cannot comment.
reviews.author: Benjamin

reviews.title: AVOID this product and company.
reviews.comment: I  thought this power supply was a great deal and got it 6 months ago. It is pretty quiet, and I like that it has eco mode. After half a year, one morning, I went to wake up my pc and it completely shut down and would not start. I had an old power supply from 15 years ago that I swapped out and everything works fine. These things do happen with pc parts, so I figured that it is at least under warranty and I can get a replacement. Unofrtunately, this is were it has been an absolute nightmare. It has been a week now since I contacted the manufacturer and they are making me essentially troubleshoot it as if I hadn't done that enough. I do so and then they tell me they want me to send a video of me doing it. Note that each time it takes at least a day to get a reply from them, even if I respond right away after receiving their email. So it's been a week, I'm using an underpowered and old PSU in my pc, and I haven't even been able to ship the PSU to them yet to start the RMA process which I can only image will take a few more weeks. It really is unfortunate, but I cannot recommmend anyone do business with them.
reviews.author: Arturas Dovydenas

reviews.title: Very nice.
reviews.comment: GeForce RTX 4070-Ti-Super, Intel 14900F, yes I play PC games and I watch streaming movies on a 4K TV.  This thing does the job. Not only does it provide 1000W, but it looks clean with its white paint job.  And, more important than the paint job, the connectors in the back of the unit allow me to pick and choose what I want to plug in.  No annoying hard-wired extra cables will get in the way here!  The unit comes with ALL the cables you'll need (assuming you're not doing something REALLY different with your PC), too.  It runs nearly silent as well. My advice:  put this inside your PC, then plug the power cord from this into a BATTERY BACKUP WITH SURGE PROTECTION.  Because you never know when a blackout, brown out, or power surge might happen.  I built a computer for my dad the same time i did my own, and he decided it's too much work to wait for the external battery/surge-protector to come in the mail so he plugged this right into the wall.  Three days.  That's all he got out of it.  Three days.  One bad ice storm (we live in Maine and it's December) was all it took.  Just a tiny flicker in the power grid as the wind shook the power lines like crazy, and ice & breaking tree branches took down several lines.  And the power supply got cooked because of it.  So I had to order a new power supply unit for him... possibly also a new motherboard & CPU but we're not sure yet.  So please, use a surge protector system behind this!!
